faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions for Travelers in Morocco
faq.q1: Do I need an international driver's license to rent a car in Morocco?
faq.a1: Most rental agencies and checkpoints accept national driver's licenses written in Latin script (EU, UK, US, Canada). An International Driving Permit is recommended if your license uses a non-Latin script.
faq.q2: What are the dress codes when visiting medinas and rural villages?
faq.a2: In urban tourist hubs like Marrakech or Agadir beach resorts, casual summer wear is fine. However, in traditional medinas, religious sites, and Atlas villages, modest clothing covering shoulders and knees is appreciated.
faq.q3: Are credit cards widely accepted, or should I carry cash?
faq.a3: Major hotels, modern restaurants, and official shops accept credit cards. Cash in Moroccan Dirham (MAD) is essential for souks, taxis, tips, small shops, and desert or mountain oases.
faq.q4: Is Morocco safe for tourists and solo travelers?
faq.a4: Yes, Morocco is generally considered safe for tourists. Watch out for unofficial guides and persistent vendors in medinas, and use official taxis or ride-hailing apps. Avoid walking alone in poorly lit alleyways at night.
faq.q5: How can I get a SIM card and internet access in Morocco?
faq.a5: You can buy a SIM card upon arrival at the airport (Orange, Maroc Telecom, or Inwi). Tourist packages are inexpensive and include plenty of data. You can also activate roaming or use an eSIM if supported.
faq.q6: Do I need a visa to enter Morocco?
faq.a6: Citizens from the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, and many other countries do not need a visa for stays up to 90 days. Always double-check current requirements based on your nationality.
